x: Skelley ran finely but could not make up his two yards deficit and Stan Blunden was close on his shoulder. The winner looks a very promising sprinter and, provided he does not overdo matters too early in the season, he should prove a very useful addition to our sprint team.
We had a very enjoyable evening's sport and the final result was very close and very satisfying so far as we were concerned. In the 100 yards we only gained 1 point and that was by Stan.
Pritchard and Stan Blunden. The 4 x 880 yards came next and with Mitcham putting their best man first against Frank Webb, the latter did well to finish about 20 yards behind his opponent.
In the 220 yards final Stan Blunden finished 2nd, and we then had the 2 Miles team race in which our team was Alf Taylor 3rd, Art Allum 4th, and Dick Tobin 7th.

Then came the final event in the senior match, this being the 220 yards, and although Stan Blunden ran well to finish a close third we were unlucky in the fact that Ted Gray had to stop near the finishing post owing to straining a muscle.

Talbot, and Stan Blunden ran the 220 stage, but at the finish we were still 5 yards behind the leaders. This made the final score: Old Tiffinians A.C. 43 pts., Belgrave H. 34 pts., Old Emanuel A.C. 4 pts.
Worrad; and in the 220 yards Stan Blunden ran a fine race, only to lose first place by inches to S.
This year we experimented with a 300 yards race, but entries were very poor, due mainly to holidays, and Alby Bird, off 10 yards, ran a good race to just beat Stan Blunden, off 6.
This Winter training has proved very useful to the following members, who ran so well last season: S. Botwright, S.
Has got his O.C. interested in running and brought a team to Mitcham for Joe Bink's last relay. Stan Blunden, now in Hampshire doing his P.T. with Sergt.
He has been supported by Frank Simmons, Stan Blunden, and our Captain. Jack Quarton has also lent his assistance in this event in addition to the Shot and Discus.

Stan Blunden ran well to win the 220 Yards, and our representatives for the 440 were Alf Shaw and Les Cohen! George Powell had a field day in winning three field events, while young Hendry showed the results of Charlie Jones' careful coaching in clearing his highest jump of the season.
We all hope that we shall be seeing you in some of the London fixtures again. Stan Blunden is now up at Kidderminster (Worcs.) and has become a proud father.
Stan Blunden writes from Kidderminster to say that he had a fairly good track season last year. Is hoping to see the lads when they are competing in the Midlands.
